# Subsets of the complex plane

The modulus and real and imaginary parts describe curves and regions in the complex plane.

Visualize the following subsets of $\mathbb{C}$. Decide which sets are open, closed, or neither.

## Exercises {.unnumbered}

::: {#exr-complex-sets-exercise level="intermediate"}

$\{ z \mid |z-1| = 1 \}$

:::

:::{#exr-complex-sets-exercise-2}

$\{ z \mid |\mathrm{i}z-1| < 1 \}$

:::

:::{#exr-complex-sets-exercise-3}

$\{ z \mid |z-\mathrm{i}| + |z + \mathrm{i}| < 4 \}$

:::

:::{#exr-complex-sets-exercise-4}

$\{ z^2 \mid |z - \mathrm{i}| = 1 \}$

:::

:::{#exr-complex-sets-exercise-5}

$\{ z \mid \Re(e^{\mathrm{i}\pi/2} z) > 0 \}$

:::

:::{#exr-complex-sets-exercise-6}

$\{ z \mid \Im(z^2) > 0 \}$

:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="tutor"}

## Solutions {.unnumbered}

### Solution to @exr-complex-sets-exercise {.unnumbered}

Square the equation and introduce $x$ and $y$ to get the equation for a circle, i.e., boundary of a circle. Alternatively just realize that the modulus $|w|$ is the distance from the origin.

### Solution to @exr-complex-sets-exercise-2 {.unnumbered}

Interior of a circle.

### Solution to @exr-complex-sets-exercise-3 {.unnumbered}

Ellipse with foci at $\pm \mathrm{i}$.

### Solution to @exr-complex-sets-exercise-4 {.unnumbered}

Parameterize the original circle by $z(t)=\mathrm{i}+e^{\mathrm{i}t}$, $0\leq t<2\pi$, and plot or analyze the image curve $z(t)^2$.

### Solution to @exr-complex-sets-exercise-5 {.unnumbered}

This is a half-plane.

### Solution to @exr-complex-sets-exercise-6 {.unnumbered}

*The source does not supply a solution.*

:::
